claims.statement: The FastAPI application mounts dashboard, plan, workflow approval, Linear, Slack, health/completion, GitHub, and sandbox-tool routers; it refuses wildcard dashboard CORS origins with credentials and validates GitHub login, sandbox, local-model, and database startup prerequisites during lifespan.
GitHub, Linear, and Slack webhook routes verify their platform signature against the raw request body before decoding it and return HTTP 401 when verification fails.
Slack claims an admitted event with claim_slack_event before scheduling normal message or update processing, so only the claimant can create or update a Slack run.
Slack blocks operations in externally shared or unverified channels; an app mention in an external shared channel receives a claimed one-time refusal reply and is not dispatched.

Outside code channels, Slack admits a normal message only when it is explicitly directed, a DM, a kitchen-channel turn, an allowed-bot invocation, or a permitted solo-thread follow-up, and it drops ineligible bot/self messages.
Slack resolves a location by preferring an explicit mapping, then metadata matches, then a deterministic ID; a conflicting mapping is surfaced as an error rather than guessed.

Slack processing requires a valid GitHub token for a human triggering user and prompts them to link or re-authenticate rather than dispatching when the token is missing or revoked; allowed bot requests use a separate path.
Slack sends explicit requests with multitask_strategy='interrupt' and other follow-ups with 'enqueue'; message edits are admitted as update processing rather than standalone normal-message dispatch.

Linear accepts only non-bot Comment create events mentioning Open SWE, resolves a repository from explicit comment text, author default, or workspace default, and rejects a result outside the allowlist.

A Linear worker derives the thread from the issue ID, persists Linear issue source context, serializes issue/comment data into typed input, and dispatches it; image-bearing input can select a vision fallback model.

GitHub routes multiplex issue, PR, comment, review, push, and CI events; they filter unsupported actions, gate workspace routing and repository/organization policy, require registered commenters and mentions for ordinary comment work, and route untagged agent-PR comments or review-finding replies separately.

GitHub PR comment processing recovers an embedded Open SWE branch UUID when present and otherwise derives a PR thread ID, resolves the user's token with one 401 refresh retry, reacts with eyes, serializes eligible comments into typed input, and triggers or queues the run.
Reviewer runs use reviewer_thread_id and assistant_id='reviewer', separating requested/automatic PR review work from coding-agent threads and graphs.

The dashboard permits lazy thread creation only for run.start, enriches it with authenticated-user attribution, resolved configuration, structured input, and invocation metadata; an active-thread run.start is steered into the live run or creates an enqueue run when requested.
Desktop execution is enabled only for source='desktop' runs whose local project path resolves to an allowlisted project or a worktree under the configured worktrees directory.

Schedules are represented by LangGraph crons targeting the scheduler assistant; a tick launches a fresh agent thread only after confirming the scheduled workspace exists and its repository remains accessible to that workspace.
Thread-id derivations are a persisted cross-process routing contract, so changing their namespaces or input strings can orphan live threads.

Input serialization enforces human/system kind alignment, XML-escapes authored content in input-message envelopes, validates namespaced entity IDs, and uses SHA-256-hashed dynamic context to avoid reinjecting context still visible to the model.
dispatch_agent_run rejects mixing a prebuilt input with raw content or identities, otherwise constructs input as needed and delegates agent/reviewer triggers to create_durable_run.

create_durable_run defaults to interrupt multitasking, sync durability, resumable streaming, v3 stream modes and subgraphs, and correlates configurable state and metadata with an invocation ID and start time.
A completion webhook is attached only when its secret is configured and its URL is absolute and non-loopback; the receiving health route fails closed on the token.

Run completion finalizes terminal telemetry/turn state, schedules eligible successful Slack cost refreshes, and for error or timeout performs best-effort reviewer/code-channel cleanup and source-specific idempotent failure replies; interrupted runs are not failure replies.
